slides.title: Entering the US market in 2027

claims.claim: Route options for the board: Amazon-led, retail-led or a Japan scale-up instead
evidence: Onsoo Botanicals; CEO and board; 2026-11-15
Synthetic benchmark data: company and figures are fictional

slides.title: Key questions

claims.claim: Should Onsoo enter the US market in 2027, and if so by which route, within an $18M cash cap, payback by 2030 and an 8% group margin floor?
evidence: Sub-questions: 1 Is the US an attractive market for Onsoo in 2027? 2 Does an Amazon-led entry meet the board's cash, payback, margin and growth objectives? 3 Would a national specialty-retail launch be the better route? 4 Does the answer survive ad cost, tariff and downside risk, and does it beat a Japan scale-up? 5 How should Onsoo launch, and what tells the board to scale, slow or stop?
Decision maker: CEO Park Ji-won with the board, choosing a route (or no US entry) for 2027

Success criteria: US cash need of $18M or less through 2030; US cash flow back to zero by end 2030; Group operating margin of 8% or more every year; On the way to $40M of US revenue by 2030; One major new-market launch in 2027
Timing: Board meeting, March 2027
Out of scope: Routes the planning team did not model; US and Japan launches in the same year

1.9x June units as a multiple of January

slides.title: 1c: US buyers rate the cream highly but come back far less often than in Korea, which keeps acquisition cost high

Against 31% for first-year skincare brands on Amazon US and 48% for Onsoo in Korea

evidence: 6% of reviews complain of Korean-only label text
The most common complaint in the pilot

Amazon-led entry meets the board's cash, payback and margin limits, but falls short of the 2030 revenue ambition

claims.claim: Each Amazon unit leaves a positive contribution after fees, advertising and landed cost
evidence: $4.7 contribution per unit at the planning team's 25% ACoS

claims.claim: Cash need peaks far below the $18M cap and is repaid in 2030; the group margin stays above the floor

slides.title: 2a: Advertising decides Amazon profitability: at $6.00 a unit it is the largest cost, leaving $4.73 of the $24 price

claims.claim: A thin margin that moves with ad cost
evidence: Rice Ferment Barrier Cream on Amazon US, $ per unit, at 25% ACoS and 15% duty: Price 24; Referral fee 3.6; Fulfillment fee 5.1; Advertising 6; Product cost 3.5; Freight 0.55; Import duty 0.525; Contribution 4.725
19.7% of the price is left as contribution

claims.claim: Advertising: each point of ACoS moves contribution by $0.24 a unit, the one cost Onsoo controls
Amazon fees: referral and fulfillment are set by Amazon and take more than a third of the price
Landed cost: product, freight and duty are under a fifth of the price, so the tariff matters less than ads (4b)
evidence: The planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs

slides.title: 2b: Amazon-led cash need peaks at about $1.9M in 2027, a ninth of the board's cap, and is repaid in 2030

claims.claim: Payback, not the cap, is the binding test
evidence: Option A cumulative US cash flow, $M, end of year: 2027 −1.94; 2028 −1.7905; 2029 −0.3165; 2030 2.39975
10.8% of the board's $18M cash cap used at the peak

claims.claim: 2027: setup and a full year of fixed cost come before volume can cover them
2028: fixed cost is covered once Amazon sales pass about $10.7M a year
2030: payback lands in the last year allowed, so any loss of margin pushes it out (4a)
evidence: How the 2030 position is built: $13.3M contribution (all 2027–30 units × $4.73) − $9.2M (fixed cost $2.1M a year and $0.8M setup) − $1.7M (inventory: four months of landed cost) = $2.4M cumulative cash flow, end 2030
Cash flow = operating result less the change in inventory

slides.title: 2b: With Amazon-led entry the group margin bottoms out at about 9.5% in 2027, well clear of the 8% floor

claims.claim: The US loss is small next to the group
evidence: Board floor 8.0%
Group outside the US: plan revenue of $140M to $158M at an 11.0% operating margin

claims.claim: 2027: the only year with a US loss, about $1.5M against $15.4M of profit outside the US
2028–29: the US turns profitable and lifts the margin back toward the 11.0% plan
2030: the margin is back above the plan outside the US, as US contribution grows

slides.title: 2c: Amazon-led revenue reaches $26.4M in 2030, two-thirds of the ambition, and is still growing 29% a year

claims.claim: On the way to $40M, two years late
evidence: Board ambition $40.0M
Share of the ambition reached in 2030: 66%
Revenue growth, 2029 to 2030: 29.4%
Revenue in 2032 if 2030 growth holds: $44.2M (2030 revenue × 1.29 × 1.29)

claims.claim: 2030: growth is still close to a third a year, so the gap is one of timing
Retail-led gets closer by 2030, but only by breaking the cash cap (3a)
The board's wording is "on the way to $40M revenue by 2030"; we read it as a direction, not a hard test, and flag it for the board to confirm

evidence: Board cash cap $18.0M
115.5% of the board's cash cap used by the end of 2030

2029–30: new doors add fixtures and stock, so the line keeps falling

evidence: Option B uses the planning team's own 4.5 units per door and 1.3x halo

claims.claim: The floor binds three years running
evidence: Board floor 8.0%

claims.claim: 2027: launch fee, fixtures and a full year of retail fixed cost land in the first year
2028–29: volume grows, but not fast enough to carry $9.6M a year of US fixed cost
2030: back above the floor only in the last year, too late for the board's test
The margin floor alone rules out a national retail launch in 2027

slides.title: 3a: To carry its own fixed cost, each door would need about 19 units a week, four times what well-known newcomers sell

claims.claim: The bar sits far above anything newcomers achieve
evidence: $7.5M retail-layer fixed cost a year (national marketing $6.0M and field sales $1.5M) ÷ 1,000 doors in 2030 = $7,500 fixed cost per door per year ÷ $7.5 contribution per retail unit = 19.1 units per door per week to break even, from 994 a year

claims.claim: Brands above 20% aided awareness sell a median of 4.6 units per door per week; break-even is 4.2 times that
Contribution per retail unit is the $14.00 wholesale price less $3.50 product, $0.75 freight, duty, 8% co-op and 4% returns
No Amazon halo is counted here; with the planning team's 1.3x halo the retail layer still loses money (3c)

slides.title: 3b: At Onsoo's awareness, doors would sell about 2.6 units a week, short of the 4.0 that keeps a brand on shelf

Retailer cut-off 4.0
1.7x the plan's sell-through as a multiple of the median at Onsoo's awareness

claims.claim: Below 10%: Onsoo's aided awareness is 4% among category buyers and 9% among K-beauty buyers
Even the top quarter of low-awareness brands sells 3.4 units, under the cut-off
evidence: Interquartile range below 10% awareness is 1.9–3.4. The leading retailer removes brands below 4.0 after 12 months
Retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 brands

claims.claim: Option B's 4.5 comes from the retailer's deck on successful newcomers, and matches brands above 20% awareness

slides.title: 3c: The 0.71 correlation shows that big brands are in more doors, not that doors create Amazon sales

evidence: Saebom added 300 doors in 2025, three years after an Amazon-first entry, once it had about $30M of US revenue
A retailer's buyer picks proven sellers, so Amazon success comes first and doors follow

evidence: Older, larger brands have bigger budgets, more reviews and more doors
A cross-section of 30 brands cannot separate the effect of doors from the effect of size
0.7 correlation of doors with Amazon sales, 30 brands

claims.claim: A real halo would still not pay for retail (Not decisive either way)
evidence: $3.98M Amazon contribution from the 1.3x halo, 2027–30
Against $31.6M of retail fixed, launch and fixture cost over the same years

Option B ends 2030 about $23.2M behind Option A

claims.claim: A fair test compares the same brand's Amazon sales before and after it enters doors

slides.title: 3d: The one recent retail-first entrant lost about $21M, while the only brand that scaled started on Amazon

claims.claim: Saebom: retail came after scale, three years in

claims.claim: Amazon-first is no sure win; a small miss costs little
evidence: Gaon Lab: Amazon-first in 2022; Stayed small; Below $5M revenue
Yeoreum: Amazon-first in 2023; Stayed small; Below $5M revenue

Ad cost is the one uncertainty that can flip the answer, and it also decides whether the US beats Japan

claims.claim: Payback by 2030 needs ad cost at or below about 28.6% of sales, under the 32% benchmark
evidence: 28.6% break-even ACoS for cumulative cash to reach zero by end 2030

claims.claim: A tariff rise to 25% would cost about $1.1M of 2030 cash and would not break the case alone
evidence: −$1.1M change in cumulative cash by end 2030 at plan ACoS

claims.claim: A stalled launch costs little: even sales stuck at $5M a year need well under half the cap
evidence: 38.8% of the $18M cap used by 2030 if sales stall at $5M with 32% ACoS

claims.claim: Japan passes the financial tests with less risk, but builds a much smaller business in a slow market
evidence: $7M Option J incremental Japan revenue in 2030

slides.title: 4a: Payback by 2030 needs ad cost at or below 28.6% of sales, yet brands scaling on Amazon typically pay 32%

claims.claim: The plan's ad cost runs against the evidence
evidence: ACoS: Plan assumption 25%; Pilot, Jan–Jun 2026 28%; Break-even for 2030 payback 28.5583%; Median, brands scaling $5–20M 32%

claims.claim: Plan, 25%: assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures; the agency benchmark says it rises as brands bid on broader keywords
Pilot, 28%: ran on a small budget; a bigger budget buys costlier clicks
Each point of ACoS moves 2030 cumulative cash by about $0.67M
Benchmark range of 26–38%: only the bottom of it pays back by 2030
Make ACoS the first gate and review it every quarter from launch

slides.title: 4b: A tariff rise alone would not break the Amazon case; ad cost at the benchmark level would, with or without it

claims.claim: Ad cost decides payback; benchmark ACoS fails even at today's duty
evidence: ACoS 25%, duty 15% (plan): $2.4M cumulative cash end 2030; −$1.9M peak; 9.5% lowest margin; Pays back
ACoS 25%, duty 25%: $1.3M; −$2.2M; 9.4%; Pays back; tariff costs $1.1M
ACoS 28%, duty 15% (pilot): $0.4M; −$2.4M; 9.3%; Pays back, barely
ACoS 28%, duty 25%: −$0.7M; −$2.8M; 9.2%; Misses payback by $0.7M
ACoS 32%, duty 15% (benchmark): −$2.3M; −$3.2M; 9.1%; Fails even at today's duty
ACoS 32%, duty 25%: −$3.4M; −$3.9M; 9.04%; Misses by $3.4M; still within cap

claims.claim: 25% duty is applied from 2027 although the ruling is expected in mid-2027, so the tariff rows are conservative

slides.title: 4c: If sales stalled at the level of two Amazon-first peers, cash need would reach about $7M, well inside the cap

claims.claim: Our worst case: no recovery and no cost cuts
evidence: −$6.98M cumulative US cash by end 2030 if sales stall at $5M and ACoS is 32%
Each year loses about $1.5M against $2.1M of fixed cost
Stall sizing: −$1.5M US result a year ($5M ÷ $24 × $3.05 − $2.1M) × 4 years − $0.8M setup − $0.3M inventory = −$6.98M

claims.claim: The gates would stop it well before 2030
Amazon-first failure is small and reversible; no board limit is breached; most of the cap stays unused
evidence: 38.8% of the board's $18M cash cap used in the stall case
Against 116% for Option B on its own plan
Far below Mooncrest's retail-first loss of about $21M

claims.claim: Cost stress (both cost risks at once) misses payback by 2030, but stays inside the cap; group margin stays above 9.0%
evidence: −$3.9M peak cash need at full plan volume with 32% ACoS and 25% duty, reached in 2029

slides.title: 4d: Japan passes the financial tests with the least risk, but builds a $7M business against $26.4M for Amazon-led

claims.claim: A and J well inside the cap
evidence: Peak cash need: A −$1.9M; B −$20.8M; J −$1.1M

claims.claim: B never pays back
evidence: Cumulative cash, end 2030: A $2.4M; B −$20.8M; J $1.8M

claims.claim: B breaks the floor
evidence: Lowest group margin: A 9.5%; B 4.5%; J 10.1%

claims.claim: Scale is the case for the US; Japan adds little growth in a market that barely grows
evidence: Revenue in 2030: A $26.4M; B $37.6M; J $7M

claims.claim: Growth sits in the US
evidence: Market behind it: A K-beauty up 89% in 2021–25; B Same market as A; J Japan grows 1.5% a year; Onsoo holds 3.1%
Option J has no inventory data in the pack, so its cash is its operating result; Option B's peak is its end-2030 position

slides.title: 4d: Japan returns more cash by 2030 unless ad cost holds at plan; the US case rests on building a bigger business

claims.claim: Japan is safer to 2030; the US is bigger after it
At plan ACoS: the US ends 2030 ahead of Japan on cash as well as on size
At pilot ACoS: the US still pays back and earns about $1.9M in 2030 against Japan's $1.3M, growing far faster
At 32% ACoS: the US misses payback and trails Japan in every year
Japan: steady, but capped by a market growing 1.5% a year
Choose the US with an ad-cost gate, and keep Japan as the fallback if ACoS stays above break-even
evidence: Japan's figures have no inventory build in the pack, which flatters its cash slightly against the US

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Approve an Amazon-led launch for 2027 with quarterly gates; add retail only once awareness passes 20%. Choose the US with an ad-cost gate, and keep Japan as the fallback if ACoS stays above break-even.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen. Meets the board's cash, payback and margin limits (peak cash need −$1.9M, payback 2030, lowest margin 9.5%) but reaches only 66% of the $40M ambition in 2030; payback depends on ACoS at or below 28.6%.

alternatives_considered.option: Option B: Retail-led national specialty-retail launch
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. Would break the $18M cash cap (−$20.8M by 2030) and the 8% margin floor in 2027–29; its 4.5 units/door sell-through and 1.3x halo assumptions do not hold; Mooncrest's retail-first entry lost about $21M.

Not chosen but kept as fallback. Passes the financial tests with the least risk but builds a $7M business against $26.4M for Amazon-led, in a market growing 1.5% a year; becomes the better 2027 choice if ACoS stays above break-even.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's initial hypothesis (Amazon-first with retail trigger at Amazon sales above $10M and awareness above 15%, ACoS falling to 25%, specialty retail from 2029)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Holds with three changes: retail trigger at aided awareness above 20%, ACoS gated at 28.6% break-even, and a targeted door test instead of specialty retail from 2029.
Left out: not modeled by the planning team; mass retail is 14% and brand websites 12% of K-beauty sales.

alternatives_considered.option: US and Japan launches in the same year
alternatives_considered.treatment: Ruled out by the board: management can run one major launch in 2027.
Named on slide 2 as a choice for the board ("choosing a route (or no US entry) for 2027"); not discussed separately.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Ad cost is the one uncertainty that can flip the answer: payback needs ACoS at or below 28.6%; plan assumes 25%, pilot ran at 28%, brands scaling on Amazon pay a median 32% (benchmark range 26–38%)
The plan assumes ACoS falls as the brand matures; the agency benchmark says it rises as brands bid on broader keywords; the pilot ran on a small budget and a bigger budget buys costlier clicks
Tariff ruling expected mid-2027; a rise to 25% duty would cost about $1.1M of 2030 cash; 25% duty is applied from 2027 so the tariff rows are conservative
The board's wording "on the way to $40M revenue by 2030" is read as a direction, not a hard test, and flagged for the board to confirm
The planning team applies the hero product's per-unit economics to all SKUs
90-day repeat is 29% vs 48% in Korea; a wider range may lift it; no data yet shows whether it will
The pilot (three SKUs) understates what a full range can do
The 1.3x halo rests on a 0.71 correlation across 30 brands that cannot separate the effect of doors from brand size
Option J has no inventory/working-capital data in the pack, so its cash equals its operating result, which flatters its cash slightly against the US
Option B's peak cash is its end-2030 position
A weaker won lowers dollar product costs; it is upside for every route and not counted
Stall case assumes no recovery and no cost cuts: sales stuck at $5M with 32% ACoS uses 38.8% of the cap
Aided awareness of 4% is among all facial skincare buyers; among K-beauty buyers it is 9%
Amazon-first is no sure win (Gaon Lab and Yeoreum stayed below $5M revenue)
Data is synthetic benchmark data: company and figures are fictional
